📋TESTING: We have activated a matchmaking test that increases maximum queue times for Plat+ players on all platforms, in all regions. The queue time increase scales with Rank tier, and Masters players could expect a maximum extension of approximately 30 seconds.

This test is in pursuit of tighter skill bands in high skill matches and less spill over of high rank players into mid-rank matches, as the matchmaker spends more time prioritizing the tightest possible lobbies before expanding its search. This test will run until the end of the season, or until we have enough data.
Please continue to give feedback on if you are experiencing tighter matchmaking.

Following early data showing promising impacts to queue times and tighter match skill-widths, we will be expanding this test to Wildcard matchmaking as well. This text expansion will be live at 10am PT, on October 16th and will impact players on all platforms in US-West.

Starting tomorrow, October 7th at approximately 10am PT, we will be conducting a matchmaking test by enabling cross-play as the default option for all players, on all platforms in the US-West servers. The intention of this test is to shorten queue times and tighten matchmaking skill bands. This test will run until the season ends on November 3rd. Console players can opt out of the test by turning off cross-play in your settings menu.

items.text: [p align="start"]Welcome back to Split 2 of Apex Legends: Marked. To start the second half of the season, we’ve got Legend balancing changes, some adjustment to loot availability (including more healing items), buffs to a trio of long range weapons, and the usual array of tweaks, fixes and adjustments. Split 2 starts on September 15th, so assemble your squad and get ready to jump back into Marked!

[p align="start"]In the leadup to Split 2, we implemented significant, new systems to detect players using unauthorized controller hardware or software in Apex Legends on all platforms including: PC, PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch 2.

[p align="start"]Prior to implementation, we spent several months thoroughly validating these systems to ensure they can accurately identify prohibited behavior. Players that trigger these detections will be actioned upon and may be banned accordingly upon review. Playing on console does not make you exempt from detection or enforcement.
[p align="start"]This is just the beginning for these new systems which we will continue to improve to keep pace with evolving cheating methods.

[p align="start"]We want the community to know that we are actively working to identify and remove cheaters at every level of play — including the highest ranks. Thank you to everyone who reports suspicious behavior and helps us keep Apex Legends fair.
[p align="start"]For more anti-cheat information, check out our most recent update!

[p align="start"]Dev note: Our main goal is to give Conduit players more avenues for skill expression and to ensure her abilities feel functional, readable, and fluid. Apex’s Shield Healer saw a big uptick in her success throughout Season 29 thanks to some overhauls to her Tactical and its associated upgrades. Despite Conduit receiving a few nerfs since then, we still wanted to come back to her this Season to focus on polishing and refining her Ultimate, as mentioned in the Season 29 Designer’s Notes. Beyond her base kit, we wanted to give Conduit two brand new Level 2 Upgrades that are now fully unique to her and emphasize different aspects of her aggressive support style.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Added preview visuals on the shield bar to indicate how much Temp Shield will be generated by the end of the regen period.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Various aspects of the Ultimate’s deployment have been smoothed out, meaning it fires faster and gets you back to guns sooner.
Can now toggle orientation while targeting to deploy jammers in a forward line.
Added a new HUD element to better inform players if their deployment location will cause jammers to break.
Also, individual jammer indicators now turn red if they would break at the current targeting location.
Jammers now spawn higher and slightly closer together, creating a tighter formation that covers more vertical space.
Jammers activate significantly faster, establishing the barricade’s threat area quicker.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Both Level 2 Upgrades, Battpack and Bigger Jam, have been removed.
NEW: Concurrency (Level 2)
Refire Energy Barricade once with no cooldown within 10s of initial firing.
Jammers spawn in a tighter formation with 2 less jammers.
NEW: Jammed Up (Level 2)
[p align="start"]Energy Barricade’s jammers have a 25% larger radius and enemies damaged by them have their HUD jammed for 10s.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Though this grenadier has seen a gradual increase in play over time since his rework in Season 28, we wanted to revisit him to address the community feedback that we didn’t hit the efficacy, impact, and responsiveness expected of a new Motherlode. We’re also making some big shakeups to his Upgrade configuration that impact the rest of his kit, including incorporating Wreckless and Knuckle Cluster into his base kit (with some nerfs). Rest assured, we’ll be keeping a close eye on him, as our intention is to add more hype tech to Fuse’s toolbox without pushing him toward being a Legend defined by his movement. He will always be Apex’s explosives expert first and foremost!
[p align="start"]Passive
Added 25% Explosive Damage Resistance at base and can see ordinances highlighted in the world within 30m of him.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Fuse can now Knuckle Jump at base.
Jumping no longer provides Tactical cooldown reduction.
Jump power moderately decreased, so Fuse will gain less momentum when jumping.
Now displays a visual indicator that signifies the radius where the jump can be activated.
Significantly decreased the time it takes to return to guns after firing.
Players can now ADS while aiming to zoom.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Slightly decreased the raise time.
Adjusted the firing arc with the focus on the main explosive projectile landing more quickly and responsively.
Added an indicator to visualize the radius of the initial and subsequent explosions.
Decreased the time it takes for the mini-bombs to explode, speeding up the rollout of explosions.
Decreased the damage falloff on the initial explosion, meaning enemies closer to the edge of the radius will take a higher percentage of the maximum damage.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Knuckle Jumper (Level 2) and Wreckless (Level 3) have been removed.
Reignition has been moved from Level 3 to Level 2.
Pyro Techniques (Level 2)
Doubled the radius of the persistent flames.
Reignition (Level 2)
Decreased Ultimate Recharge Rate from 1s per 2 explosive damage to 1s per 3 explosive damage.
NEW: Big Bang (Level 3)
Knuckle Cluster’s explosions cover a 50% larger area.
NEW: Sticky Bomb (Level 3)
Knuckle Cluster’s initial projectile is 25% larger and sticks to enemies. Every 7 hits on an enemy reduces Knuckle Cluster’s cooldown by 1s.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Catalyst saw a small boost in pick rate after her buffs in Season 28, but we felt she needed more love using a slightly different approach since her stats didn’t hold. This Season, we’re focusing more holistically on smoothing out the tension of moving from base to base amongst the fast pace of action. We want Cat’s building experience to be fun and flexible, so giving her more options to customize her space and adding in some longtime community-requested quality-of-life features will empower players to feel rewarded for putting in the work to master her. We’re also making big swings on shuffling up her upgrades, including a new Level 3 upgrade, Ferro-Frenzy, that will really shake up how we see players approach their setup.
[p align="start"]Passive
Catalyst is no longer immune to other Catalysts’ abilities.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Now automatically reinforces or rebuilds doors if colliding with a valid door or doorway on placement.
Decreased Cooldown from 20s to 15s.
Increased Spike Height, meaning that players can less easily jump over them.
Hitting enemies with the projectile will now deal damage to them.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Significantly decreased firing time, making it smoother to deploy and raise the wall.
Allies are no longer slowed or blinded when passing through the wall.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Sole Piercer (Level 2) has been removed.
Hidden Spikes has been moved from Level 2 to Level 3.
Resilient Veil and Ferro-Door have been moved from Level 3 to Level 2.
Ferro-Door (Level 2)
Now also increases max reinforced doors from 4 to 6.
Resilient Veil (Level 2)
Now also decreases Ultimate Cooldown from 150s to 120s.
NEW: Ferro-Frenzy (Level 3)
Your max Spike count is increased by 1. Spikes are 50% smaller, but deal faster tick damage.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Bloodhound got some significant changes for this season but they haven’t been as impactful on their pick and encounter win rates as we hoped. With these updates we’re hoping to add some improvements to their Ultimate and Tactical. We’ll continue to monitor Bloodhound’s performance and adjust if needed.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Reduced cloak visibility while in dome.
Ring damage no longer drops cloak.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Added 1 extra second on scan length.
Tweaked to provide more frequent snapshots, but the snapshots fade over time.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Sonar snapshots begin fading more quickly.
Sonar snapshots should disappear more readily when seeing the head of either the snapshot or the player being tracked.
[p align="start"]Back to Top

[p align="start"]Dev note: For an ability with a short cooldown that can have a devastating effect on one target, the Kickstart drone needs more counterplay options. Even when the victim decides to destroy the drone, the high health pool often makes that hard to do, especially in close quarters when Axle is quickly following up, herself. For cases when destroying it isn’t an option, at least the victim should be able to have more agency about where they get displaced with the knockback nerf and decreased stun.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Nitro Gate launch speed reduced from 750 to 700.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Ultimate HP reduced from 200 to 150.
Base Ultimate cooldown increased from 90s to 120s.
Ultimate knockback arc widened and max height reduced.
Ultimate stun duration reduced from 1.5s to 0.25s.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Jump Gate replaced with a new Drone Deployer Upgrade that brings the Ult cooldown back down to 90s.

[p align="start"]Dev note: The turn slow punishment on the Seer tactical was very frustrating to fight against. We’ve decided to remove the turn slow since the tactical output is still strong without it.
Removed turn slow when hit by the Tactical
[p align="start"]Back to Top

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Last season, we made a huge change to loot distribution and spawning (read our retrospective in this update’s designer’s notes!). After reviewing the data and feedback from the community, we are making some minor adjustments to healing, ammo, and weapon availability. Healing was becoming scarcer than intended, and due to the removal of energy ammo, the other ammo types were spawning ammo boxes at higher rates than intended.

[p align="start"]Bin Resets have been adjusted to be closer to its pre-Season 30 version but keeps the original intent of reducing its overall spike to player power. The Season 30 version was not providing the density of necessities needed to quickly re-stock for the end game. Reset Bins now have more items on average with healing, ammo, survival slot items, and amps spawning more frequently inside.

[p align="start"]The Weapon Assist feature previously only included a small selection of pistols, shotguns and the Alternator. To help players find higher quality weapons off the drop, we are expanding this to now include all available weapons.

[p align="start"]These adjustments help to address some of the pain points we have been seeing while maintaining the overall goal of last update’s changes of creating an overall healthier loot curve as the game progresses.
[p align="start"]We will continue to monitor your feedback and make adjustments as quickly as we can!

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Season 30 was a large shakeup to the weapon meta and we want to let things settle a bit more before making any big changes. We are buffing a few weapons that were previously falling behind and have continued to fall after Season 30.

[p align="start"]Dev note: In this patch, we’re rolling out over 150 map-related Quality of Life fixes across the Outlands with a massive chunk of that polish going straight to World’s Edge. We’ve smoothed out sticky collisions to keep wall-bouncing and rotations fluid, patched up geo holes that were occasionally swallowing loot and Legends, and permanently closed off several unintended rat spots to maintain competitive integrity. Alongside these tweaks we’ve also cleaned up some clipping issues related to Alter’s Ultimate.

[p align="start"]Massive shoutout to our community for continuing to report these back to the team. Finding every hole, ledge or rat spot across the Outlands is a huge undertaking and the clips and bug reports you share are exactly what helps us track them down. Your feedback directly shapes the map health of Apex so keep sharing your clips.

[p align="start"]Welcome to the latest season of Apex Legends: MARKED. In addition to Bloodhound’s rework, buffs to Loba and Rampart, an energy weapon systems overhaul, and brand new Corrupted Attachments, we’re also bringing you a World’s Edge map rework, quality of life tweaks, and a slew of balancing changes. All of this is in pursuit of evolving Apex Legends into the best, most competitive Battle Royale out there. This season is going to push you and your squad to be the best you can possibly be, so get ready to group up, gear up, and dive into MARKED when it drops on August 4th, 2026!

[p align="start"]In Season 29, we ran two matchmaking tests — 1-Tier Premade Restrictions and Diamond+ Solo-Queue-Only — to experiment with variables to potentially use to address player frustrations in Ranked. Thank you to everyone who engaged with the tests and for the feedback you provided; it’s integral to helping us shape the future of the game mode. We are actively analyzing and evaluating the data from these tests, and are in the process of writing an upcoming blog to discuss the results and next steps. Keep an eye out for the followup comms in the coming weeks.

[p align="start"]We've beefed up our servers in Season 30. While not everyone will notice the difference, many players should experience increased stability, less lag, and lower chances of slo-mo servers across all game modes and regions. We're always working to improve the competitive experience for our players and, while these changes often take place behind the scenes, we’re excited to provide a noteworthy improvement for you all!

[p align="start"]Dev Note: We feel World’s Edge is in a solid place competitively, and have seen the sentiments echoed throughout the community, so our focus in updating the map was reducing disparity between POIs and delivering on players’ frequently requested changes, such as the return of Sorting Factory and Construction Stacks. To complement Bloodhound’s rework, we leveraged the new POIs in this update to move Bloodhound’s story forward in a meaningful way.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Over the lifetime of Apex, Looting has changed substantially. A rising problem we wanted to address with these changes was the loot inflation and ease that players have around finding very high quality loot. In many cases, progressing through a match could feel like a quick spike at the beginning or mid point of the match and quite flat afterwards.

[p align="start"]We’ve overhauled several systems that were added over the past few years to shape a more engaging and straightforward loot chase for players. The spawn rates of high tier loot have been reduced across all maps, meaning that finding a rare Attachment will be a ‘rarer’ occurrence, and will signal a real shift in the power of your weapon.

[p align="start"]Arsenals provide a consistent way to get the guns you want, but can disrupt the game start by luring players into hot drop contests in the open spaces around Arsenals. Arsenals are now time locked, similar to EVO Harvesters. This ensures that they are available early game when you want them, but that your earliest fights off the drop are supplied only by what you can loot from the map. Unique loot sources such as Wildlife, Vaults, MRVNs, Ticks, and Rollers are still present but provide reduced quality of loot.
[p align="start"]TL;DR: Spawn rate of high tier loot has been reduced across all maps, which should shape a clearer and more cohesive looting experience.

[p align="start"]Dev note: We are updating how Weapon Stats are shown in game to improve transparency and readability of gameplay in Apex. You can now explore with greater detail than ever the unique stats and performance characteristics of each weapon. By exposing these stats and allowing players to examine how different attachments impact weapon performance, players can make more informed choices in-game quickly. Presenting this greater information with visual refinements is part of our effort to improve Onboarding and clarity of gameplay for all players.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Corrupted Attachments provide players with a meaningful choice when they are equipping their guns. Providing a unique blend of big buffs and negative stat trade offs will reshape a weapons performance and specialize its power. Limited to one Corrupted Attachment per weapon, players must make tactical decisions about their preferred loadouts. Need an absolute bullet hose for those close range fights? Put the Overflowing Mag on the R-99 for easier one-clips at the cost of longer reloads. Or do you want more maneuverability and speed? Put the Agile Standard Stock on the R-99 instead for increased movement speed at the cost of reduced mag size.

[p align="start"]Dev note: We're taking a big swing with energy weapons this season and really shaking up their ammo systems. We've removed energy ammo entirely as a lootable item. The goal of this change was to provide another way to think about your weapon loadout choice, and why you are picking one weapon over another. To lean into their unique energy identity these weapons will now come with their own regenerating ammo pool. Removing the need to hunt for extra ammo or spend valuable inventory space opens up new loadout opportunities, but keep an eye on that stockpile - once it's run dry players will have to wait for it to regenerate. With replenishing ammo, we expect energy weapons to be most powerful in shorter fights, but start to lose ground in longer sustained engagements.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Core to Apex is the Drop Ship experience, it is not only the game’s start, but it also influences a team's odds for success. A successful jump can be the difference between a top placement in a match and a quick trip back to the lobby. Timing and positioning your team for a good Drop is a skill check, and it is a responsibility that some players prefer to have in their direct control. Volunteering for Jumpaster empowers the more experienced and adventurous players who want to shape the start of their team’s game.

[p align="start"]In game modes with a Jumpmaster, during Character Select, players can now volunteer to be Jumpmaster. This adds a deterministic way for players to take on the responsibility of being the Jumpmaster for their team.
[p align="start"]During Character Select
When Volunteering is active, players will see an option to ‘Opt In To Jumpmaster’.
Players can press the corresponding button to Volunteer at any time during Character Selection.
Players who have Opted In to Jumpmaster will be marked on the UI in Character Select.
Players who volunteer for Jumpmaster on a match will be Opted In to Jumpmaster for future matches.
Players can use the same button press to Opt OUT of volunteering if they have previously Opted IN.
If more than one team member has Volunteered, Jumpmaster will be selected randomly from the group of Volunteers.

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Despite changes to Bloodhound’s kit in Season 28, they remain nearly invisible at middle-to-high tiers and have the lowest pick rate once you get to Gold tier and above. Luckily, we teased additional changes, and it’s finally time to show off Bloodhound’s refreshed kit. The biggest change is a brand new Ultimate, Allfather’s Cloak. This is a multifaceted cloaking tool that will help your squad ambush opponents or escape third-party situations. Combined with easier-to-use tracking tools from your Passive and Tactical, it’s much easier to gain an understanding of the battleground and then push in when enemies show weakness. The hope is that Bloodhound players feel like they can now play from the front foot, leading their squad and creating openings instead of just scanning some enemies and hoping your allies can take advantage.

[p align="start"]Dev Note: While this season’s looting changes should improve Loba’s value as she improves her team’s loot quality, we felt like she could use some buffs to help improve her ability to stay alive and support the team. Her tactical deploys much faster, and her ultimate cooldown is being reduced to make sure she can continually deliver the goods to her squadmates.

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Despite significant buffs, Rampart still has trouble competing in the current meta. She can be extremely strong if she gets bunkered up in a good position, but it is otherwise difficult to make work. Her Passive can be underwhelming depending on the strength of LMGs, so we’re adding a new layer. We’re also improving her mobility with Sheila to help her in fights against more mobile opposition.

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Valk has remained in the upper tier in terms of pick rates for several seasons now. As we continually try to level the playing field, it feels like time to reduce Valk’s power level. There are two main goals - reduce her “artillery” power, which rivals other characters who don’t have jetpacks, as well as make her Ultimate a bit easier to counter.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Base damage reduced from 25 to 15 (each additional rocket still does 3 damage)
Adjust the missile’s attack angle as they approach their target
This reverts an element of her Season 27 changes, where the missiles were able to fly over tall walls or buildings and dive straight down on top of players
[p align="start"]Ultimate

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Axle’s pick rate has been trending in a healthier direction with each subsequent nerf, however, we understand her Kickstart drone is still too oppressive in too many contexts. On Axle’s release, players had the option to access double Tac or double Ult charges. Nitro Gates and Kickstart Drones have been everywhere, and it’s given everyone plenty of opportunities to learn how to use (and how to react) to her kit. Her Tac can help her entire team quickly close a gap. Her Ult can launch victims into the air. The strength of those outputs is not lost on us, and some of the changes over the season have simply been to limit the availability of some strong abilities. Other changes have been attempts to expand counterplay opportunities or change the context of when her abilities are strongest. The nerfs in this season are in the vein of the latter; we’ll see how Axle-related fights are affected and, if she’s still a menace to deal with in too many situations, we’ll take an even more heavy handed approach.

[p align="start"]Dev note: We have seen the frustrations surrounding Seer – his Tactical can feel oppressive, and is being encountered at an increased rate – and are continuing to address them. The changes we’ve made so far have been meant to reduce the frequency with which you'll encounter Seer's Tactical. At split start, the most picked Upgrades (2 Tac charges / reduced Tac cooldown in Ult) saw ~90% and ~80% pick rates, respectively. When combined, players have access to 2 Tac charges on a very short cooldown. By moving both to level 3, players can only have one. These changes have helped address complaints of Tactical spamming in Ult, while keeping the intended power of those two Upgrades in place. As we discussed in our most recent Designer's Notes, Seer is a tricky Legend to balance, as a prominent Seer meta is an oppressive one. We will also reduce the amount of turn slow so you shouldn’t feel like you’re stun locked.

releases.displayName: Apex Legends™: Overclocked Midseason Patch Notes

items.text: [p align="start"]Welcome back to Overclocked Split 2! To start the latter half of the season, we’re bringing Legend balancing changes, new shotgun hop-ups, and various fixes and improvements that we think you’re going to like a lot. With all these changes landing on June 23rd, it’s the perfect time to grab your squad and dive into Overclocked!

[p align="start"]We cannot overstate the value we put on competitive integrity in Apex Legends; hopefully you’ve seen our incremental and seasonal recap account ban updates. We have also been working hard behind the scenes to eradicate less conventional hacks. This season, we implemented detection for a reverse speed hack, preventing cheaters from freezing themselves mid-air for long stretches of time. Additionally, we identified and resolved numerous exploits that could be used to take down servers. Combatting cheaters is a constant cat and mouse game, as such, we are not always able to discuss all the things we’re working on, lest we tip our hand to bad actors. Rest assured, we are committed to making Apex Legends the cleanest it can possibly be, and we are working on things that we’re excited to be able to share with you soon. Please continue to report suspected cheaters, your reports help inform our anti-cheat work!
BALLISTIC

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Ballistic has been strong in the past but after a bunch of nerfs he’s fallen close to the bottom in pickrate. We wanted to bring some of his power back but we understand he was pretty frustrating to fight against in his prime. This goal with his Tactical buff is to bring back some of the previous numbers but we wanted to add more counterplay options for the victims. The speed boost on the Ultimate was also very powerful but it could make Ballistic’s team very difficult to fight. Instead, we’re only giving a sprint boost which should still allow for fast pushes as a team but not a speed advantage during the fight.
Passive
Ballistic now respawns with his Sling weapon in all game modes.
Tactical
Overheat now only applies to one weapon.
If a player has a weapon out when hit by Whistler the overheat debuff applies only to that weapon.
If the player is unarmed when hit by Whistler it applies to the weapon in the first weapon slot.
Overheat no longer degrades when not firing or swapping to another weapon.
Overheat does not increment when swapping to another weapon and shooting.
Overheat damage increased from 15 to 50.
Overheat debuff duration increased from 12 to 15.
Tactical charges increased from 1 to 2.
Decreased time between firing and when homing activates.
The overheat debuff no longer re-applies if you hit someone who is already overheating and you cannot apply it to multiple guns on the same player.
Ultimate
Ballistic and teammates within range get a sprint boost when his Ultimate is activated. (Previously only Ballistic got a speed boost)
Sprint boost will only apply a speed boost while sprinting and will not speed up other types of movement.
Upgrades
Level 2
Extra Bullet: Gain an additional Tactical charge.
Trap Mode: When placed in the world, Ballistic’s KTactical lasts 15 seconds and deals 35 damage if an enemy walks into it.
Level 3
Quiet Time: Ballistic’s Tactical no longer applies overheat. Instead it adds silence and slow on hit. It also has a longer cooldown.
Killing Time: Now moved to level 3, still provides a 15 second extension to Ballistic’s Ultimate.
PATHFINDER

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Your favourite friendly robot has been a bit outclassed by other skirmishers. We wanted to touch the uptime on his abilities to help him keep pace and improve his Upgrades to be more in line with other Legends that get perks from other classes.
Passive
Pathfinder now tucks in his legs while riding horizontal ziplines.
This should make him a little harder to hit when riding on his Ultimate and other ziplines in the world.
Tactical
Tactical charges increased from 1 to 2.
Removed the progressive cooldown and it is now a flat 20 seconds.
Ultimate
Increased launch speed of the zipline projectile.
Reduced cooldown from 3 minutes to 2 minutes.
Upgrades
Level 2
Field Research: Now grants all Recon perks instead of just the survey beacon scan.
Ringmaster: Now grants all Controller perks instead of just the ring console access.
Level 3
Landing Gear: Grants more air control and faster recovery from hard landings. This replaces the 2 Tactical charges Upgrade.
SEER

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Seer saw a bit of an uptick after his last set of buffs but has settled back down toward the bottom. He is, however, seeing some play in higher Ranked lobbies so we know he has potential. For this update we focused on quality of life buffs. We’ve done a pass on making his Passive and Tactical more responsive.
Passive
Increased the activation speed of the heartbeat sensor.
Decreased the interval time between heartbeats.
Decreased activation time for unarmed ADSing
Made the delay when aiming more consistent between weapon and unarmed.
This means the heartbeat sensor will appear at the same time regardless of the weapon you’re using.
Tactical
Reduced the delay between the launch and hit.
Improved the slow on hit, should now halt faster moving Legends more effectively.
Ultimate
Upon deployment, there is now a quick 2 second scan of the area which will highlight any enemy in the area.
Enemies that enter the area after it’s deployed will also be scanned for 2 seconds.
Cloaked enemies will now show footsteps if they are within the Ultimate zone.
AXLE

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Axle has undeniably pushed the pace of play. With these nerfs, we want to target areas that cause the most frustration while staying true to her identity as an aggressive lateral speedster with team utility. Considering the popularity of her “Super Slider” upgrade, her Tactical has simply been available too frequently, nullifying much of the risk that should be considered when overextending. We also saw an opportunity to add some agency to Kickstart victims, when evading or destroying the drone simply isn’t an option.
Tactical
Reduced max in-world count from 3 to 2.
Reduced hp from 150 to 100.
Passive/Tactical

Knocked players can no longer slide across zip codes as Axle or while under the effect of a Nitro Gate. They can still boost through a Nitro Gate, but once the effect times out, they will slow down accordingly.
Upgrades
"Super Slider" Upgrade no longer grants a second Tactical charge. Instead, it now grants Nitro Gate a 5 second cooldown reduction and +1 max in-world count.
Ultimate
Kickstart now displaces victims on a parabolic arc based on their velocity at the moment of impact, instead of straight up.
Reduced enemy highlight duration slightly to better match stun duration.
MAD MAGGIE

[p align="start"]Dev note: Maggie has been a top performer for a while and, with the rise of Gibby, she’s seeing even more play. She is doing a lot and her Tactical is completely controlling the battlefield. Her Ultimate creates an issue similar to previous-era-Ballistic, where the added speed boost is making players very difficult to lock down. In this case, we’re introducing a series of nerfs to bring her pick rate down to a more healthy space.
Tactical
Increased Cooldown from 22 seconds to 28 seconds.
Ultimate
The speed boost granted from running on the pucks dropped by the wrecking ball has been replaced by a sprint boost.
Will no longer speed up all movement, just when sprinting.
VALKYRIE

[p align="start"]Dev note: Valkyrie is becoming one of the top picked Legends and has been performing really well over the last few seasons. We are making a minor adjustment to help assuage frustrations and manage her climbing pickrate. We understand this doesn’t address other aspects of her kit that are strong, but we are continuing to monitor her match data and will make additional changes if necessary.
Passive
Removed the recent improvement, which allowed her to land faster from skydiving.
CONDUIT

[p align="start"]Dev note: Since her changes at the beginning of Season 29, Conduit spiked to the top of the pick rates and remained at that spot several weeks later. We’re so excited to see that players have really felt the improvements to Conduit’s supportive agency and playmaking potential. However, we recognize that she has been a key enabler of Legends that push the meta in an extremely aggressive way. Additionally, her dominance crowds out all other Support Legends, making her an obvious pick. Finally, she was present in 8 of the top 10 most popular team compositions. All of these indicators point to an unhealthy balance state and, as a result, we want to take steps to slow things down a bit.
Tactical
Decreased Regen Rate from 15/s to 10/s
Increased Regen Duration from 6s to 8s
Decreased Ally Total Regen from 90 to 80
Decreased Conduit Total Regen from 60 to 56
Upgrades
Level 3
Instant Barrier: Increased Regen Duration from 4s to 6s
Tactical
Increased Cooldown from 27 seconds to 30 seconds
Upgrades
Level 3
Enduring Barrier: No longer grants regen through ring damage

[p align="start"]Dev Note: The Hemlok Breach AR has stayed pretty dominant in the meta since its release, even through a few rounds of adjustments. Its damage per magazine has always been pretty generous, so the following change aims to tone down the dominance at higher tiers.
Hemlok Breach AR
White magazine reduced from 21 to 20
Blue magazine reduced from 24 to 22
Purple and gold magazines reduced from 27 to 25
EVA-8
Small increase to handling speed.
Mozambique
Small increase to handling speed.
[p align="start"]Dev Note: We’re introducing a new hop-up and juggling around another, for all the information about why check out our latest edition of Designer’s Notes.
Executioner \
Available on: Peacekeeper and Mastiff
Knocking an enemy with the weapon grants 50 shield regeneration over 10 seconds
375 points to unlock

Removed from: Mastiff

Removed from: Peacekeeper

Removed from: Longbow DMR, Wingman and Mozambique
Added to: Flatline and Volt

[p align="start"]Dev Note: It’s been a while since Nemesis has seen some updates from us, so it’s time… Turbo Nemi has arrived. The weapon will become fully heated after two bursts, allowing it to fire at its maximum fire rate much quicker.
Turbocharger
Added to: Nemesis \[600 points to unlock]
